pages.name: Survival Activities
pages.html:
Survival & General Hazards

The following procedures are basic survival activities spacers may need to do to stay alive. Each survival activity lists sample skills and characteristics that can be used for any necessary checks, but the referee is free to alter the listed suggestion based on the decisions of the spacers.

Book p.106

pages.name: Healing and Recovering
pages.html:
Healing and Recovering from Injury

Healing and Recovering from Injury: Healing requires treatment and time for a character to heal from any wounds they have sustained.

  • First aid: END at 0 requires a successful medic skill to recover 1 END to allow the character to start healing naturally. This must be done within 10 minutes of reaching 0 END.
  • Surgery: If END and STR or DEX is 0, then the character requires surgery to start healing naturally. Not receiving surgery within 1D hours will cause a loss of -D3 of the remaining characteristic every hour until they receive surgery.
  • Natural healing: All characters recover 1 wound in STR, DEX, and END per day of rest as long as END isn’t at 0.
  • Medical-assisted recovery: Medication can help accelerate recovery. In addition, resting in a medical environment such as a hospital where the character will be under medical supervision doubles the natural healing rate.

Book p.106

pages.name: Building Shelter
pages.html:
Building Shelter

Building Shelter: Having shelter is important to prevent exposure from the elements. Not having shelter will cause the spacers to take damage equal to the listed amount on the Weather table.

  • END or STR + Survival Rank + Terrain DM per 6 hours spent building.

Book p.106

pages.name: Food and Water
pages.html:
Food and Water

Food and Water: Spacers require sustenance every day to maintain their health. A character can survive for two days without rations before gaining adverse effects from a lack of food and water.

  • After 2 days, incur -1 END per additional day without food and water.
  • A human character needs a minimum of 500g of food and 2000g (2 liters) of water per day.

Rations can be easily purchased in any settlement. All rations provide the minimal amount needed.

  • 1 day of provisions weighs 500g and costs 5cr.
  • 1 day of water rations weighs 2000g and costs 5cr.
  • Rations may cost more based on the location as determined by the planetary code.
  • Provision cost is doubled per interval above Population code A.
  • Water cost is doubled per interval of Hydro Code below 3.
  • Survival kits provide 5 days of food rations and 5 purification tablets, which purify 2 liters of water each.

Book p.106

pages.name: Hunting
pages.html:
Hunting

Hunting: If needed, a spacer can go hunting to harvest rations. To determine the animal, use the Alien Animal generator on pages 110-113 to determine the size of the animal.

  • END or DEX + Survival Rank + Terrain DM per 6 hours spent hunting. Hunting produces 1 ration per hit the animal had. For example, an animal with 12 hits provides 12 rations.
  • Optional: Roleplaying the Hunt: When hunting, the check can be used to determine an animal encounter which will then be played out in combat if the spacer engages.

Book p.106

pages.name: Foraging
pages.html:
Foraging

Foraging: Similar to hunting, spacers can forage for food but also for water. However the spacer must indicate whether they are foraging for food or water.

  • INT or EDU + Survival Rank + Terrain DM per 6 hours spent foraging. The amount foraged 1D per Survival rank, modified by terrain DM.

Remember: When foraging, six hours pass so an encounter check must be made by the referee.

Book p.106

pages.name: Scavenging
pages.html:
Scavenging

Scavenging: Scavenging is similar to foraging but is applied when searching for non-consumable resources for survival purposes or crafting. The spacer should state what their intended objects / material they are looking for and their intended purpose before they go scavenging. For example, if the spacer is looking for firewood to make a fire, then they must state their intent.

  • END or INT + Survival Rank + Terrain DM per 6 hours spent scavenging.
  • Remember: When scavenging, six hours pass so an encounter check must be made by the referee.

Book p.106

pages.name: Crafting
pages.html:
Crafting

Crafting: Crafting is applied when spacers are looking to create something for the material they have on hand that could be essential to survival. For example, this roll is made when converting a hunted animal carcass into consumable rations or making hunting weapons. Typically this would be done using the crafting skill, however with survival it is assumed the spacer is lacking a suitable workshop or resources needed and is instead using what they have on hand or what they can find.

  • Crafting takes 6 hours of time.
  • Important: Crafting is open-ended and is subject to the ruling of the referee with regards to the characteristics, skill, and environmental factors. Use the other example survival activities to help determine the DMs for a crafting roll.

Book p.106

pages.name: Know Direction
pages.html:
Know Direction

Know Direction: To prevent getting lost on a planet or when searching the wilderness for a point of interest, it is important that the spacers have a sense of directional orientation to prevent becoming lost.

  • EDU or INT + Survival Rank + Terrain DM + Weather DM to prevent becoming lost. Using appropriate tools can provide additional benefits, as the referee determines.

Book p.107

pages.name: Gravity and Falling
pages.html:
Gravity and Falling

Gravity and Falling: Falling can be debilitating for spacers if they are not careful, especially when factoring a planet’s gravity.

  • 0.25G or less (planet size 1-3): 1 damage per 2 metres falling.
  • 0.5G (planet size 4-6): D3 damage per 2 metres falling.
  • 1G (planet size 7-9): 1D damage per metres falling
  • 1.5G (planet size A-B): 2D damage per metres falling
  • 2G+ (planet size C+): 3D damage per 2 metres falling.
  • Note: Armour does not mitigate falling damage.

Book p.107

pages.name: Vacuum Exposure
pages.html:
Vacuum Exposure

Vacuum Exposure: The vacuum of space is extremely hostile to most life forms. Vacuum exposure normally only happens if someone is unwillingly ejected into space without a vaccsuit on.

  • 1 damage per second in a vacuum
  • Vaccsuit Puncture: if a vaccsuit has been punctured or compromised, then vacuum exposure causes d3 damage per 6-second round. Vaccsuits can be temporarily sealed with vacctape.

Book p.107

pages.name: Poison
pages.html:
Poison

Poison: When exposed to poison, the spacer makes an END check. On failure, the damage and poison effect immediately affects them. Additional END checks are made per interval, with a success negating the poison before the damage and poison effect occurs and neutralizing the poison until exposed again.

Poison LevelTypeEND check difficultyDamageInterval
1Minor+0DM1D plus effect (roll d3)Per day
2Major-1DM2D plus effect (roll 1D)Per hour
3Severe-2DM3D plus effect (roll D3+3)Per minute

Book p.107

pages.name: Poison Effects
pages.html:
Poison Effects

Poison Effect: Use the following table to determine the poison effect.

  • Determining poison effect: If needed, roll the dice associated with the poison type to determine the effect.
  • Effect duration: Each poison type lasts until a successful END check. This check is made at the beginning of each interval.
1DPoison Effect
1Illness: -2 DM for feeling fatigued and nauseous
2Tranquilizing: Knocked out until a successful END check
3Confusion: Must make a successful INT of 8+ to attempt to perform any Skill. Failure means the spacer forgets what it is and cannot attempt to perform the Skill.
4Paralysis: Cannot move until a successful END check.
5Neurological: D3 + poison level of INT damage.
6Necrotic: 1D damage to either DEX or STR.

Book p.107

pages.name: Fatigue
pages.html:
Fatigue

Fatigue: Incur -2DM to everything after doing one of the following.

  • Lack of sleep: Being awake for more than 18+ END. To remove the penalty, rest a number of hours equal to END plus every extra hour awake.
  • Heavy labour: Performing heavy labor for a number of hours equal to more than END. To remove the penalty, rest a number of hours equal to END.
  • Combat: Making melee attacks over END. To remove the penalty, rest for a number of minutes equal to END to recover.

Book p.107

pages.name: Carry Weight
pages.html:
Carry Weight

Carry Weight: A player may be impacted by how mobile they are due to the amount they are carrying.

  • Minimal: A character can carry their x2 STR characteristic in kilograms without impact.
  • Encumbered: X3 STR in kilograms, reduce combat movement distance and combat endurance by 50%.
  • Over-Encumbered: x4 STR in kilograms, reduce combat movement by 75% metres and they cannot sprint or make melee attacks. Walking for long periods while over-encumbered will incur fatigue as they are performing heavy labour.

Example: Dmitri has an STR of 8. He can carry up to 16kg without penalty but is considered encumbered if carrying between 17-24kg. Dmitri is over-encumbered if he carries 25-32kg and cannot make melee attacks or sprint.

  • Worn Items: Clothing does not count towards weight, but wearing armor or vaccsuits applies 50% of their weight to encumbrance.
  • Encumbrance and movement: A spacer’s overland movement is reduced by -1kmh for every 1kg over their maximum carry weight.

Book p.107

pages.name: Radiation
pages.html:
Radiation

Radiation: Radiation is a lingering threat in space, on thin atmosphere planets, and from certain power sources. Spacers don't have to worry about rad exposure while inside their spaceship, but vaccsuits have a maximum amount of rads they can protect against before needing to be rinsed in a de-radiation bath.

  • Vacuum rad exposure: In the vacuum of space, assume 10 rads of exposure per hour to an individual. In the presence of solar flares, roll 2D and multiply it by 10.
  • Atmosphere rad exposure: On a low atmosphere world (type 1), assume 1D per hour. Worlds with more substantial atmospheres have negligible rad exposure.

There are two factors to consider with regard to radiation when exposed.

  • Immediate effect: The amount of rads exposed they have been exposed to will deal a level of damage. This damage is immediate only.
  • Cumulative effect: Rads will build up overtime if not treated, leading to long-term impact on END.

Radiation should only be tracked if the spacer has ongoing exposure without protection from radiation, such as a leaking power plant on their ship, damaged starship shielding, or exploration of a radiated wasteland without proper protection.

The following table illustrates the range from minor to extreme radiation to help adjudicate dealing with radiation in your game.

  • Damage from immediate exposure: This damage happens immediately after exposure. Track number of rads to determine long term effects. If someone passes from one level to another, they will also take that damage immediately.

Exposure to Radiation Table

LevelDescriptionExampleAmount (Average)Damage from Immediate Exposure
1MinimalLow atmosphere/general space1D rads/hour (10 rads/day)None
2LowMinor reactor leak/solar flareD3 x 10 rads/day (30 rads a day)D3
3MediumMajor reactor leak/major solar flare1D x 10 rads/hour (60 rads/hour)1D
4HighUnshielded radioactive material or waste2D x 10 rads/hour (100 Rads/hour)2D
5SevereRadioactive weapon2D x 10 rads/minute (100 rads/minute)4D
6FatalNuclear epicenter4D x 10 rads/second (200 rads/second)8D

Distance from Radioactive Source: When exposed to a radioactive area, use the radiation level to determine how many range bands away a person can be before becoming exposed.

  • Example: A minor reactor leak (level 2) affects an area of two range bands.

If someone enters within the range, they will be exposed at radiation level 1. If they keep approaching the source of radiation, then the radiation level increases until they are at close distance to the radiation source and are thus exposed to their maximum radiation level.

  • Example: A minor reactor leak (level 2) will deal level 1 radiation at 5-10 metres and then deal level 2 radiation in close range under 5 metres away.

Rads: The amount of rads a person has in their system will permanently destroy their END over time due to rads building up and staying in their bodies. The following table describes the effect of rads and their cumulative level of damage to the body.

RadsEND DamageImmediate Physical impact
0-150NoneNone
151-300-1 ENDIllness
301-500-2 ENDHair loss
501-800-3 ENDRadiation burns
Over 800-4 ENDNeurological disruption

Removing Rads: A person will naturally remove rads from their body after six months from exposure, at a rate of 1D x 10 Rads a month.

  • Medical Intervention: TL8 - TL10 worlds will have medication or treatment that allows for the removal of 1D x 10 rads in one week. TL11+ worlds can offer the removal of 1D x 10 rads in a day with treatment.

Protection from Radiation: The following allows for protection from radiation up to its listed amount. This means these items prevent any radiation exposure regardless of length of time. Once the rad amount exceeds the protection level of the items, then subtract the protective amount per interval of exposure. Examples of items that provide protection:

  • Vaccsuits and Battledress: TL x 10 rads protection
  • Starship Hull: 500 rads protection
  • Prevents D3 x 10 rads a day.

Book p.108
